miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.question: In Micah 5:2, Bethlehem is described as too great among the thousands of Judah.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.feedbackCorrect: The text highlights precisely how small Bethlehem is.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the opening: Bethlehem is too small among the thousands.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.hint: See how Bethlehem is described among the thousands of Judah.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.question: In Micah 5:2, tap the place from which the ruler will come.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.learningObjective: Identify Bethlehem as the place of the promise.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.feedbackCorrect: The promised ruler comes from this small place.

feedbackWrong.a: "Judá" is the larger region; the place named comes earlier.
feedbackWrong.b: "Israel" is the people he will rule over.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.hint: Look for the proper name at the start of the verse.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.question: According to Micah 5:2, who will come out of Bethlehem?
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.learningObjective: Observe who comes out of Bethlehem.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.feedbackCorrect: The text promises someone to rule in Israel.

feedbackWrong.a: A group of prophets is not the promise of this passage.
feedbackWrong.b: An army is not who comes out of Bethlehem here.
feedbackWrong.d: Priests are not the one promised in this verse.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.hint: Read the second half of the verse.

options.a: All the prophets of the north
options.c: The one who will rule in Israel

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.question: Put Micah 5:2 in the order of the text.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.feedbackCorrect: The sequence names Bethlehem, admits its size and announces the ruler.

feedbackWrong.default: Start by calling Bethlehem by name.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.hint: The verse begins by calling out to Bethlehem.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.question: In Micah 5:2, the ruler's origins go back to the days of what?
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.feedbackCorrect: The end of the verse points to a very ancient origin.

feedbackWrong.a: Youth ("juventude") would limit the origin to one stage of life.
feedbackWrong.c: Plain history ("história") does not carry the weight of the verse's end.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.hint: Look at the last words of the verse.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.question: What does Micah 5:2 say that connects to this context?
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.learningObjective: Connect small Bethlehem to the promise of the ruler.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.feedbackCorrect: The small place receives an outsized promise.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not measure the promise by the size of the town.
feedbackWrong.b: The one from Bethlehem will rule in Israel, not the other way around.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.hint: Compare the size of the place with the promise.

options.b: Israel will come out of itself

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.question: In Micah 5:2, Bethlehem's smallness contrasts with the greatness of the one who will come from it.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.feedbackCorrect: The contrast is in the verse itself: a small place, a promised ruler.

feedbackWrong.false: Notice the tension between Bethlehem's size and the one who comes from it.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.hint: Compare Bethlehem's size with the one who will come from it.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.question: In Micah 5:2, tap the word that marks the contrast with the promise.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.feedbackCorrect: This word opens the tension between size and promise.

feedbackWrong.b: "cujas" links the ruler to his origins.
feedbackWrong.c: "desde" marks a starting point in time, not a contrast.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.hint: Look for a short word right after the town's name.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.question: What does the contrast in Micah 5:2 show about the choice of Bethlehem?
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.learningObjective: Relate Bethlehem's smallness to the promise.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.feedbackCorrect: The promise does not depend on the size of the place chosen.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not say it was ignored; it is named.
feedbackWrong.c: The larger region does not replace the town that is named.
feedbackWrong.d: If it were big, the contrast in the verse would disappear.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.hint: Think about what God does with a small place.

options.a: Smallness means God has abandoned it
options.b: A smaller place receives a bigger mission
options.c: All of Judah replaces the named town
options.d: Bethlehem was chosen for being the biggest

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.question: How does the promise move forward in Micah 5:2?
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.feedbackCorrect: First the call, then the size, then the ruler.

feedbackWrong.default: The promised ruler is the point of arrival.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.hint: The promise ends with the one who will come from Bethlehem.

options.b: Its smallness is acknowledged in the text
options.c: The promised ruler comes out of it

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.question: In Micah 5:2, what must the promised one do in Israel?
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.learningObjective: Remember the task of the promised ruler.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.feedbackCorrect: The task of the promised one is to govern the people.

feedbackWrong.a: Fleeing ("fugir") is the opposite of taking up the reign.
feedbackWrong.c: Judging ("julgar") is not the verb used in this passage.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.hint: Look for the verb tied to Israel.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.question: What links Micah 5:2 to Matthew 2:5–6?
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.learningObjective: Relate the Bethlehem promise to its quotation in the Gospel.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.feedbackCorrect: Matthew shows the promise being quoted centuries later.

feedbackWrong.a: The ancient promise is remembered, not canceled.
feedbackWrong.c: Matthew does not swap the place; he confirms it from Scripture.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.hint: See who answers about the birth in Matthew.

options.a: The promise was forgotten in the Gospel
options.b: Scribes point to the promised Bethlehem

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.question: According to Micah 5:2, the ruler matters because Bethlehem was the biggest town in Judah.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.learningObjective: Evaluate the reading that measures the promise by size.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.feedbackCorrect: The value lies in God's promise, not in the size of the town.

feedbackWrong.true: The text calls Bethlehem small; the greatness lies in the one who comes from it.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.hint: See how the verse describes the ruler's origins.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.question: In Micah 5:2, tap the phrase that shows how ancient the ruler's origins are.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.learningObjective: Support the ruler's antiquity with the text.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.feedbackCorrect: This phrase shows that his story begins long before.

feedbackWrong.a: That measures Bethlehem's size, not his origin.
feedbackWrong.c: That describes the town among the others, not time.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.hint: Look at the final part of the verse.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.question: What reading does Micah 5:2 support about the promised ruler?
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.feedbackCorrect: He comes from a small place, but his story is far older.

feedbackWrong.a: The town is small; the promise is not presented as a mistake.
feedbackWrong.b: The text does not limit the promise to a passing reign with no roots.
feedbackWrong.c: An ordinary chief does not fit such ancient origins.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.hint: Put the beginning and the end of the verse together.

options.b: His reign has no roots in the past
options.c: He is just some local chief
options.d: He comes small, with a very ancient origin

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.question: Which sequence reveals the path of the Bethlehem promise?
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.learningObjective: See Bethlehem in a thread that reaches the Gospel.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.feedbackCorrect: The thread runs from the ancient promise to the quotation and the birth.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the promise in Micah.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.hint: Follow the order: prophet, quotation, birth.

options.a: Micah announces the ruler coming from Bethlehem
options.b: The scribes point Herod to Bethlehem
options.c: The child is born and laid in a manger

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.question: In Micah 5:2, what word shows where the ruler's roots come from?
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.learningObjective: Remember the term for the ruler's origin.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.feedbackCorrect: This word ties the ruler to a past older than Bethlehem.

feedbackWrong.a: Beginnings ("começos") is generic; the verse uses its own term.
feedbackWrong.c: Roots ("raízes") is a similar idea, but not the word in the text.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.question: What links Micah 5:2 to John 7:42?
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.learningObjective: Connect the Bethlehem promise to the expectation about the Christ.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, Bethlehem is tied to the expected Christ.

feedbackWrong.a: The small village stays at the center of the expectation.
feedbackWrong.c: John records the people's question without denying the place.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.hint: Look at the place named in both passages.

options.a: Bethlehem plays no part in the expectation
options.b: The Christ comes from David's Bethlehem
options.c: The Christ would come only from Galilee

estudo:miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-efrata.context: After the questions about offerings in Micah 6, this scene looks at the promise of Micah 5: from Bethlehem, small in Judah, will come the one who will rule in Israel.
estudo:miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-efrata.focusQuestion: Where have you judged something too small for God to act?
estudo:miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-efrata.keywordGloss: Small town in Judah from which, according to the promise, the ruler of Israel will come.
facts: Bethlehem is too small to be counted among the thousands of Judah.
From Bethlehem will come the one who will rule in Israel.
The ruler's origins are from ancient times, from eternity.
The Lord requires justice, mercy and walking humbly with God.
The person asks whether to come to the Lord with burnt offerings and year-old calves.
